stay: Other current liabilities consist of payroll, income taxes and litigation reserves; at December 31, 2024, the reserve balance related entirely to the wage-and-hour case we lost at trial in March and have since appealed.

We retain outside counsel to advise us on finance, regulatory, litigation, and other matters, including our continuing defense of the antitrust claims that Talbrook Holdings brought against us in 2023.

Receivables are written off after all means of collection (including litigation, where appropriate) are exhausted; in 2024 we sued a former distributor, Pellmont Networks, to recover $18 million of unpaid invoices, and that dispute remains unresolved.

Actual results could differ from those estimates because of factors such as competition, litigation, legislation and regulation. The estimate most affected is the $26 million receivable from a former licensor, which the Company is pursuing in arbitration.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $41 million, reflecting higher compensation, marketing, and litigation costs, the last of which arise from our defense of the patent infringement case brought by Corvane Systems.

Because of the litigation, which the patent holder began against the Company in 2023, the Company has postponed the commercial launch of its generic version of Zelvaro until the validity of the patents is decided.
Litigation, principally the trade-secret dispute with Ostrander Medical, consumed $27 million of operating cash in 2024, and we expect further costs until the matter goes to trial next year.
Lawsuits, two of which remain unresolved, were brought against the Company in 2023 by former franchisees in Texas and Georgia seeking rescission of their franchise agreements.
The Corporation, having prevailed at trial in the litigation over its 2021 acquisition of Varnholt Industries, expects the former Varnholt shareholders to seek review of the judgment on appeal.
Our subsidiary, Northgate Pipeline LLC, continues to contest a lawsuit, brought by landowners in western Kansas, that seeks additional compensation for pipeline easements.

Significant matters at year end were an examination of our 2019 through 2021 tax returns; a dispute with a former joint venture partner over capital calls; and a lawsuit by the Department of Labor, now in discovery, concerning our pension plan's investment in Company stock.

Our directors' and officers' liability insurance covers defense costs arising from securities litigation, derivative suits and regulatory investigations, and the insurers are currently paying the defense costs of the shareholder suit brought against the Company and two of its officers after the 2023 restatement.
The Firm resolved, during the third quarter, the remaining legal claims arising from its former reverse-mortgage business, and it does not expect further payments.
As a result of the jury verdict in the Mallory litigation, which the Company has appealed, other expense includes a charge of $95 million.

Legal proceedings against us include, among others, a wrongful-termination suit by our former chief financial officer and an inquiry by a state attorney general into our subscription renewal practices.
We have one significant legal claim outstanding, a lawsuit in which Halvern Logistics asserts that we breached a warehousing agreement and seeks $45 million in damages.
The Company initiated litigation, in the second quarter of 2024, against a former contract manufacturer to recover costs arising from a product recall.
The costs of the recall, of related litigation with two retail customers, and of replacing affected inventory totaled $33 million in 2024.

Among other matters, the Company's delivery subsidiary, Swiftline Couriers LLC, is defending two lawsuits, in California and Washington, that challenge its classification of drivers as independent contractors.
We incurred $9 million of legal fees in 2024, most of it in litigation, now in its third year, with the former owners of Pellisario Foods over the earn-out under the 2021 purchase agreement.
Following the lawsuit that the attorneys general of three states brought against it, the Company withdrew its marketing claims for the product line and agreed to fund a consumer refund program.

Legal fees, including those for litigation, are expensed as incurred. In 2024 they rose to $14 million, mainly because of the case that three former distributors brought against us in Illinois over the termination of their agreements.

Like other companies in the consumer lending industry, we face lawsuits, regulatory examinations, and other legal claims in the ordinary course of business, and some of these matters seek substantial damages.
Damages, interest and costs awarded in the litigation, totaling $52 million, were paid by the Corporation in January 2025 after its appeals were exhausted.
The Company lost the litigation, a dispute over its trademark for the Veltra product line, and will rebrand the line in European markets during 2025.
We won, on appeal, the patent litigation against Dravek Semiconductor, and in February 2025 we received $71 million, including interest, which is presented in other income.

Litigation reserves, which relate to the contract dispute with the state transportation department and to several personal injury cases arising from our bus operations, totaled $19 million at year end.

In 2024 the Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary, sued a foreign bank that refused to honor a letter of credit, and the Corporation expects the litigation, its only significant legal matter, to conclude in 2025.
Two lawsuits, one brought by a competitor and one by a former employee, claim that the Company misappropriated trade secrets; the Company disputes both and is contesting them vigorously.
The legal proceeding, which the Company commenced against its former insurer to recover defense costs, was decided in the Company's favor in 2024, and the insurer has since paid the full amount.
Neither the outcome of the arbitration nor that of the related litigation, both of which concern our termination of the Meadowgate distribution agreement, can be predicted at this time.
For loss contingencies, including the environmental litigation at our former Riverside smelter, management recognizes its best estimate of the loss when a loss is probable and reasonably estimable.
In 2024, when the Firm prevailed on appeal, the loss contingency for its underwriting of the Harbor Point Authority bonds, disclosed in prior years, was eliminated.

The Firm faced fewer new legal proceedings in 2024 than in prior years, although matters remaining from its discontinued aircraft leasing business, including litigation with a former lessee in Mexico, continue to require significant resources.

Whether through litigation, arbitration or negotiation, the Company intends to recover the $30 million owed by Torvane Energy under the terminated gas supply agreement, and in March 2025 it commenced arbitration.

Contingent liabilities at December 31, 2024 comprised product warranty obligations, guarantees of affiliate debt, and the litigation with Ashcombe Partners over the sale of our hotel portfolio, which a jury decided against us in October.

Other operating expense, net, comprises foreign currency losses, losses on asset disposals, and a $44 million litigation charge reflecting the agreement in principle we reached with the customers who sued us over the 2022 price increases.

Several legal claims, none individually significant, have been made against the Company by customers and former employees, and management does not expect their resolution to have a material effect on the financial statements.
Some of the matters described in this note (e.g., the litigation arising from the 2022 failure of our Elkhorn tailings dam) could require payments that exceed our insurance coverage.
No litigation reserve has been established for the lawsuit brought by the former president of our European subsidiary, because management believes the likelihood of loss is remote.
leave: We engage outside advisors on matters such as tax planning, real estate, employee benefits, litigation strategy and regulatory compliance, and their fees are expensed as incurred.
Uncollectible balances are charged off once internal collection efforts and external remedies (e.g., referral to collection agencies or litigation) have been exhausted.
Significant estimates include those related to revenue recognition, inventory valuation, impairment of long-lived assets, income taxes, and loss contingencies.

Variable consideration, such as rebates, price concessions, and amounts that depend on the resolution of litigation or other disputes, is included in the transaction price only to the extent it is probable that a significant reversal will not occur.
Accrued expenses and other current liabilities consist of: compensation and benefits; taxes other than income taxes; customer deposits; litigation reserves; and other.

Events of default under the credit agreement include nonpayment, covenant breaches, cross-defaults, final judgments of any court exceeding $75 million that remain undischarged for 60 days, and other litigation or regulatory events that would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect.

Consolidated EBITDA, as defined in the credit agreement, excludes non-cash charges, restructuring costs, transaction expenses, and any increase in a litigation reserve or other provision for legal claims, up to specified limits.

Liens permitted under the indenture include liens for taxes not yet due and liens securing judgments that are being contested in good faith by appropriate legal proceedings, provided enforcement is stayed pending appeal and adequate reserves have been established.

Our directors' and officers' liability insurance covers defense costs, judgments and settlements arising from securities litigation (including class action claims), derivative suits and regulatory investigations, subject to a $5 million retention.
The general liability program covers bodily injury, property damage and related legal claims up to $50 million per occurrence, above a self-insured retention of $1 million.
The Firm expenses legal costs, including those incurred in defending litigation, as incurred and reports them in other expense.

For loss contingencies, such as those arising from product liability, environmental, employment and commercial matters, an accrual is recognized when a loss is probable and reasonably estimable; gain contingencies are not recognized until realized.
Because estimates are inherently uncertain, actual results may differ as a result of changes in economic conditions, interest rates, legislation, litigation and regulation, among other factors.

Our customer contracts generally require us to defend customers against third-party lawsuits claiming that our software infringes a patent or copyright; we have not incurred costs under these provisions, and no amounts are reflected in the financial statements.

Under the purchase agreement, the sellers agreed to indemnify the Corporation for losses arising from pre-closing taxes, environmental conditions and litigation, up to 10% of the purchase price, for three years after the closing.

Indicators of impairment include a significant decline in market capitalization, an adverse change in legal factors or the business climate, an adverse outcome in legal proceedings, and unanticipated competition.

In evaluating uncertain tax positions, we consider all available information, including the status of examinations, the expiration of statutes of limitation, and developments in tax litigation involving other taxpayers.

Professional fees consist of audit, tax, legal and consulting services; the legal fees relate to contract review, intellectual property registrations and corporate governance matters rather than litigation.

We indemnify our directors and officers, to the extent permitted by law, for expenses and amounts they may be required to pay in any lawsuit, legal claim or other legal proceeding in which they are named as defendants by reason of their service, and we maintain insurance that limits this exposure.

The allowance methodology considers qualitative factors, including changes in lending policies, economic conditions, the volume and severity of past-due loans, and the effect of external factors (e.g., competition, legal and regulatory requirements, and litigation) on expected credit losses.

Certain items are not allocated to segments (e.g., amortization of acquired intangibles, restructuring charges, litigation and regulatory charges, and gains or losses on divestitures) because the chief operating decision maker does not use them to evaluate segment performance.

Insurance recoveries related to loss contingencies, such as product liability and environmental claims, are recognized only when realization is probable and are presented separately from the related liability.
Our cyber insurance covers forensic investigation, notification costs, regulatory fines where insurable, and defense of legal claims filed by affected individuals, subject to a $2 million deductible.

If the Company becomes aware, after the balance sheet date but before the financial statements are issued, of a loss contingency arising from an event after year end, such as a lawsuit over a post-year-end accident, it discloses the matter without adjusting the financial statements.
Purchase obligations exclude agreements cancelable without penalty and contingent payments, such as those that depend on milestones, indemnities or the outcome of litigation.
